commits.title: Two sandbox purges never hold their locks together

changes.how: A custom migration: pnpm exec drizzle-kit generate --custom --name purge_sandbox_one_at_a_time, then node scripts/prune-snapshots.mjs. Its SQL is `create or replace function commerce.purge_sandbox(p_sandbox uuid) returns integer ...` with the body copied character for character from supabase/migrations/20261111172839_baseline_1_schema.sql lines 15374 to 15424 (keep language, security, `set search_path` and every option of the original) and ONE new first statement after `begin`: `perform pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('commerce.purge_sandbox'));`. Do not edit the baseline file. After the function, repeat the original's `revoke all on function commerce.purge_sandbox(uuid) from public;` and any grant the baseline gives it (lines 33565 to 33570). The signature does not change, so code that is running during the deploy keeps working.

Add a case `two purges started together both finish`: make two expired sandboxes the way the case at line 330 makes one (`made("purge")` and expiry), then `await Promise.all([sandbox.purgeSandbox(a, { remove: async () => true }), sandbox.purgeSandbox(b, { remove: async () => true })])` and expect both results to be numbers (not null, no throw) and both sandboxes' rows to be in state 'purged'. Add to src/db/sandboxes.test.ts one assertion that the function's source (`select prosrc from pg_proc where proname = 'purge_sandbox'`) contains pg_advisory_xact_lock.

Under the Purge paragraph (line 211) add the lock arithmetic: one purge runs a delete on each of about 400 store tables per round, at least two rounds, and its transaction holds about 2,130 relation locks (each table and its indexes), measured on 12 November 2026; a transaction-level advisory lock makes purges run one at a time, so the most held at once is one purge's; the lock table has max_locks_per_transaction × (max_connections + max_prepared_transactions) slots. Leave the two production numbers as a line `Production: max_locks_per_transaction = ?, max_connections = ? (read on <date>)` and fill them from the after-deploy check. State the rule: if a purge's locks come above a quarter of the slots, split the purge into parts of 50 tables (finding DS-11 step 3), and not before.
